source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Extending H&K's proposal to denominal verb formation in Sakha
notes: For instance, -LAA can attach to the bare N kuorat ‘town’ resulting in the syntactic verb kuorattaa ‘town-verb’. This verb can be well-formed all by itself as in (14a): no further arguments need to be introduced. In this case it will receive the interpretation of a weather verb leading to semantic oddness. Whereas with nouns like ‘snow’, ‘rain’ and the like, weather interpretation is fine as shown in (14b), with other nouns it is not felicitous, at least in the world that we live in. In an imaginary, fairy tale situation where towns fall from the sky (14a) would be acceptable.
